text:
If you're chasing one more dry, sunny day before the pattern turns, today's it. Morning sunshine gives way to increasing high clouds, but it stays warm and just moderately humid with a high near 86 and light south winds, all the models agree there's essentially no rain to worry about. Air quality's good, UV is strong at midday, so plan shade breaks if you're out for a while. The lake's sitting at a comfortable 76 with light waves, 1 to 2 feet, and south winds 10 to 15 knots, that's a solid swim and paddle day, best before the breeze builds toward evening.

Sunday's the pivot: showers and a few embedded storms move in after 3pm, and the forecasters are watching a slow-moving flash flood threat that lingers into Sunday night, though the heaviest rain now looks to stay northwest into Canada. Vermont should see lighter totals, a tenth to a quarter inch, nothing like the original worry. Good waterfront window today runs right through the evening; for Sunday, get your outdoor plans done before early afternoon and keep half an eye on the sky after that.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST: BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - The first day of August will feature pleasant weather for today with morning sunshine followed by increasing high clouds. It will be warm and moderately humid with highs in the 80s. Sunday and Monday will feature active, wet weather, though it’s looking less impactful than originally forecast. Showers will move into New York Sunday morning, possibly spreading into western parts of Vermont. There is the chance for a thunderstorm, but severe weather isn’t expected. However, some heavy downpours are possible Sunday night, though the heaviest rain is now expected to remain to our northwest in Canada. Parts of New York may get up to an inch of rain with isolated flash flooding not out of the question in the St. Lawrence Valley. Smaller amounts are expected for Vermont and New Hampshire.
